findings.title: The empty-commit check writes .git/index: `git diff --quiet HEAD --` refreshes the stat cache even under GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0
findings.recommendation: The walk's fix for the MM/AD empty commit compares the working tree with HEAD through `git diff --quiet HEAD --`. That worktree diff refreshes the index's stat cache and writes .git/index, and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 (which PrRunner sets precisely so `git status` does not do this, src/core/pr/run.ts:172) does not stop it. `orbit pr commit` therefore writes inside the repository, against `orbit-pr-lifecycle`'s `The orbit pr command observes and prints; it never writes`, and a user's concurrent git command can meet index.lock. select.ts's existing `diff --quiet HEAD <target> -- <path>` compares two commits and is unaffected. No test caught it: the harness checks the allowlist, not that the repository is unchanged. Whichever option is taken, make engine() assert .git/index is byte-identical (or mtime-identical) across every engine call, and show that check able to fail on the current code.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Replace the worktree diff with a read-only per-path comparison: for each non-`??` porcelain entry, compare the HEAD blob and mode (`git ls-tree HEAD -- <paths>`) with the working-tree file's content hash (`git hash-object -- <path>`, never `-w`) and its presence and executable bit; add `hash-object` without `-w`/`--stdin` writes to the allowlist row and run.ts's gitAllowed, recapture the git contract, and keep the MM/AD and untracked-only tests.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Keep `git diff --quiet HEAD --` and amend the allowlist requirement to name the index stat-cache refresh as the one write `orbit pr commit` makes (content unchanged), with its index.lock interaction as a named limit.

recommendation_options.label: C
recommendation_options.body: Revert to printing the commit on any porcelain entry and make the MM/AD case a named limit: the printed commit fails with nothing to commit and the step-failure row shows the recovery (re-opening the external finding as a limit).

findings.reproduction: In a scratch repository (git 2.55.0): commit f, wait, `touch f`, wait, record .git/index's mtime; `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git status --porcelain -z` leaves it unchanged; `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git diff --quiet HEAD --` exits 0 and .git/index's mtime changes (WRITTEN).

walk_entry.title: A nonempty porcelain status does not guarantee a commit after staging

findings.recommendation: In the same replacement, say plainly that workflows already read the change's status at their end to decide whether to run the next command, so one more read-only check is the same kind of addition.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-11T19-51-18Z.json, row 3: decided's "no longer commit" reads as verify and explore committing today
findings.recommendation: Write a replacement saying checking a change's work and thinking a change through do not commit at their own end (they never have); what they write is committed at the next of the five commands.

findings.recommendation: Write a replacement whose citation or wording carries the refusal where it is stated (the branch preconditions at propose), or that says the cited requirement applies those preconditions without restating the refusal as its own.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-11T19-51-19Z.json, row 2: decided leans on git's recorded default branch for the remote
findings.recommendation: In the same replacement, say in plain words when a repository knows its main branch (when it was cloned, not when the remote was added by hand).

findings.recommendation: Write a replacement saying that when pushing is turned on, orbit pushes to the change's own branch on the remote the project resolves, and that orbit itself does not re-check the remote, so a remote that lost commits is only noticed at the next commit.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-12T16-24-39Z.json, row 1: decided uses "a push never forces" undefined

findings.recommendation: Write a replacement defining the closing commit (the commit step at a command's end) and saying which record (the propose record orbit writes) the recovery commits.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-12T18-52-47Z.json, row 4: why presents the commit as a step the cited baseline row already names

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-12T18-52-48Z.json, row 3: decided and why misname the named limit and read "offered" as asking the user

findings.recommendation: Write a replacement whose answer says orbit init writes the setting that gives one program pull request per architecture doc.

commentary: This pass verified the two walks of the blind pair. Three edits landed as claimed: the commit step's new bullets (non-zero exit, degraded with or without a segment), the stopped-PR-layer clause and its scenario, and their carriage into the requirement, design D3, docs/customization.md and CLAUDE.md. The residual check over 5f45b7a0..HEAD found no edited file outside the walks' edit records. The engine edit for the empty commit is right in what it decides — MM and AD print no commit, an owed push still prints, both mutation-checked — but how it decides breaks the subcommand's read-only promise: a worktree diff refreshes the index even with optional locks off. A scratch repository showed it; the harness's allowlist check could not, because the call is allowlisted. The reading step's findings cluster in two shapes: records that state how orbit commits today more broadly than it does (only under a pull-request setting, and also at review handoff), and two records this walk wrote whose wording outruns what they cite or names the limit wrongly.
